surfBiteReport: The most recent surf fishing reports for the PCB-to-30A Gulf front are approximately 3 weeks old (July 2026). With water at 85°F and baitfish thick along the beaches, predators are actively following the schools — Spanish mackerel, whiting, redfish, and jack crevalle are the primary surf-zone species being landed from the sand. Whiting are the most consistent producers, best targeted with sand fleas, shrimp, or Fishbites worked in the deeper troughs between sandbars rather than cast to the horizon. Spanish mackerel and ladyfish are cruising the beachfront and can be intercepted with fast-retrieved spoons or small metal jigs, especially when birds are working bait near the surface. Fishing peaks sharply in the first few hours after daylight and again in the last two hours before sunset; midday heat pushes most fish deeper or off the bite entirely.
